solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Primate's an important person with great standing westwards

indicators.note: in an across entry, going westwards means the letters run right to left, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a person of high standing
big means great in size

explanation.surface: A primate is described as a bigwig who stands tall, facing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing westwards' turns NOBBIG round to read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The gibbon is a small tree-dwelling ape, and apes belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Thin material in work uniform accepted by Sister

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: uniform means all the same

explanation.surface: A nun's work uniform made from some flimsy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very fine, filmy fabric, the archetype of delicate cloth.

clue.text: During break, record advert about European city

indicators.note: one piece happens during the other, so it is placed in the middle of it

parts.note: to bust is to break

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the record and advert are read backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
ad is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: In a commercial break, an advert for a European city plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EPAD into DAPE, which goes inside BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, on the Danube.

clue.text: Listen! Little weight's apparent over six months?

indicators.note: the weight is seen spread over the other piece, covering it on both sides

parts.note: oz, the ounce, is a small unit of weight
six months is half a year, and half of the word year gives these letters

explanation.surface: A query whether a slight weight gain shows after half a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six months' is half of YEAR, its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier's cry calling for attention means hear ye, an exclamation asking for silence.

clue.text: A racket's produced by disturbance over in slaughterhouse

parts.note: a bat is a racket, as in table tennis

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for disturbance is read backwards

parts.note: a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: Noise from a commotion carries across an abattoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RIOT into TOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a place where animals are killed for meat, a synonym.

clue.text: Just bay horse briefly relaxing on the trailer

indicators.note: relaxing suggests letters loosening out of their order and reforming
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the phrase goes

parts.note: a trailer is a short advertisement for a film, an ad

explanation.surface: A bay horse takes it easy pulling a trailer behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts BAYHORSE to BAYHORS; 'relaxing' rearranges it to BYASHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by a short head means barely, by the narrowest racing margin, so only just.

clue.text: English runner in casual top, half-exposed

indicators.note: only half of the garment is shown, its front four letters

parts.note: a tee shirt is an informal top

explanation.surface: An English athlete jogs in a casual top that only half covers them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river: the Tees flows through north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords call a river a runner; this one rises in the Pennines and reaches the North Sea.

clue.text: One's outside light on for work

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet light
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone flicks on the outdoor light to get to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives the outside of One, O and E; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is an artist's body of work, or a single piece of it.

clue.text: Oriental fellow in desert's warm again

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
E stands for East, the Orient
he refers to a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: An Eastern man in the desert is heating up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is the verb, as in deserting a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat leftovers is to heat them a second time.

clue.text: Make pitiful money in Asia, restricting tot

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: the sen is a small coin in Japan and other Asian countries
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Restricting a child's pocket money in Asia makes for a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sadden someone is to make them sorrowful, a fair sense of pitiful.

clue.text: US sportsman to remain before game in part of changing facilities?

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the washroom word

parts.note: a bath is found in the changing rooms of a sports club

indicators.note: before puts this piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: to be is to exist or remain
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: An American athlete stays on in the locker room before the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe Ruth was a celebrated American baseball player of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: One praises director etc's filmmaking equipment

parts.note: someone who applauds or praises is a clapper
a board is a company's directors as a body

explanation.surface: A director applauds the film crew's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' suggests film, but means a company director on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapperboard is snapped shut at the start of each film take to sync sound and picture.

clue.text: Sound equipment used by Durham psychologist

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A researcher in Durham uses audio gear for experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Amps are amplifiers, which boost the signal in a sound system.

clue.text: Greek character starts to hobble about on mountain

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the first piece after the second

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone limps about on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Callas doesn't need intro for song

indicators.note: no introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Maria Callas was a famous opera soprano

explanation.surface: A great diva needs no introduction before singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, a Callas speciality.

clue.text: Physician collects green ornamentation

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so the doctor's letters hold the other piece

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
eco means environmentally green

explanation.surface: A doctor picks up some green decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decoration and furnishing style of a room.

clue.text: Charlie regularly hit out after personal data revealed

indicators.note: after puts the letters picked out behind the first piece

parts.note: ID is identification, one's personal details

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Charlie lashes out once his private details are leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name; in British slang a charlie is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a right charlie is British slang for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Father's on a holiday that's ridiculously dear — March, in America

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first piece after the holiday

parts.note: Easter is a spring holiday
pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests the letters are absurdly scrambled

explanation.surface: Dad's on a trip that's absurdly expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is a procession, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's Easter Parade is a famous festive procession down Fifth Avenue, a march in the US.

clue.text: Western street in Paris grey when described by bird

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the bird encircles the other letters

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A Parisian street looks grey as a bird describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a Western film starring John Wayne.

clue.text: In command after dynamic raid at sea

indicators.note: after places the command letters at the end
dynamic suggests lively movement of the letters

parts.note: IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A naval officer takes charge after a bold raid at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Novelist Jack takes Porsche with Dan, tearing around circuit

parts.note: J is jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: around puts the scrambled letters round the circuit letter
tearing means racing wildly, and the letters are flung about

parts.note: a circuit is a loop, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Jack and Dan race round a track in a Porsche.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad was the Polish-British author of Heart of Darkness.

clue.text: Refusal by mum to increase meal

parts.note: no is a refusal
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
to up is to increase

explanation.surface: Mother says no to larger portions at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is the word for keeping quiet, not mother. A nosh-up is British slang for a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is British slang for a large, hearty spread of food.

clue.text: Did model, in audition, deserve heavenly body?

parts.note: an artist's model sat for a portrait

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for deserve is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to earn is to deserve

explanation.surface: A model asks whether an audition earned a celestial part.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Sports venue's toilet round back

indicators.note: back means the toilet and round letters together are read in reverse

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: The stadium's loo is round the back.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an elliptical playing field, like the Oval cricket ground in London.

clue.text: Sub from United stole limelight ultimately

parts.note: U is short for United in team names
a boa is a feathery stole or scarf

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A United substitute grabbed the spotlight in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a football replacement; here it is a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, and sub is short for submarine.

clue.text: Weird headless deity is a mythical creature

indicators.note: weird says the letters are in a strange order
headless means the first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A strange god without a head is a monster of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' cuts DEITY to EITY; 'Weird' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary abominable snowman of the Himalayas.

clue.text: I've turned fifty — head covering needed

indicators.note: turned means the letters are switched around into another order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone turning fifty decides a headscarf is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a piece of fabric worn over the head or face.

clue.text: Spread bit of butter on middle of crepe

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cook spreads butter in the middle of a pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is a savoury paste served as a spread on toast.

clue.text: Medic's energy transfixes poet seen by A + E initially?

indicators.note: to transfix is to pierce, so the energy letter goes through the poet

parts.words: poet seen by A + E initially
parts.note: the poet A. E. Housman, author of A Shropshire Lad, had the initials A and E
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A doctor in Accident and Emergency attends a stricken poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A + E' looks like Accident and Emergency, but they are the poet's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain, now called a foundation doctor.

clue.text: Copier's component has run out inside

indicators.note: inside places these letters within the word for component

parts.note: a part is a component
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A photocopier part has run out of toner inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copier' is a mimic, not an office machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a bird that mimics speech, so someone who copies others is said to parrot them.

clue.text: Slightly flushed woman mixed drink

parts.note: pink is a mild flush of colour in the cheeks
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A woman blushes lightly over her cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pink Lady is a cocktail of gin, grenadine and egg white.

clue.text: Early fall leads to Irish colt getting infected

parts.note: fall is the American autumn, and September, abbreviated Sept, is its first month

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of each of the next words

explanation.surface: An Irish colt gets an infection after a fall early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is the autumn, not a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound is one infected by bacteria.
